AFDOKX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
415 AM EDT Sun Mar 15 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes were made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Lighter winds and mainly dry conditions through this evening.

2) A frontal system brings periods of showers, potentially strong
and gusty winds late tonight through Monday night.

3) Localized minor coastal flooding and localized beach erosion
possible Monday into Monday night.

4) Possible brief mix with snow very early Tuesday with
otherwise a drier and colder airmass settling into the area
Tuesday into Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

.KEY MESSAGE 1... 
High pressure already making its way out into the Atlantic. Dry
low levels will keep a mainly dry day. SE winds and increasing
clouds will keep the temperatures on the cooler side today with
highs mainly in the 40s to near 50.


.KEY MESSAGE 2... 
A developing warm front approaches tonight and moves across into
early Monday. SE winds increase tonight and will make for slowly
rising temperatures tonight. With the low level warm air
advection will come more rain showers. 

The rain showers will become more periodic and intermittent
Monday. It does not appear to be a total washout kind of rain
forecast. There will be some lulls in the rainfall. With the
warm air advection and rises in dewpoints, have also added in
fog into the forecast, with most areas along the southern
coastlines of Long Island for Monday morning. Winds will 
continue to increase and become more gusty, especially Monday 
afternoon. The area gets into the warm sector Monday afternoon.
Instability elevated will increase and make for a chance of
thunderstorms.

For Monday night, an associated strong cold front approaches and
moves across. Instability and more vertical forcing will make
for a continued chance of thunderstorms. Rain showers will
become more numerous and heavy in intensity as the front moves
within closer proximity. Peak gusts forecast during the evening
hours, potentially in and around a line of showers and embedded
thunderstorms forecast to move across from west to east.

Late Monday night, winds become more westerly behind the cold
front. Colder air will advection in. It is possible that
precipitation could end as a rain and snow mix with some areas
north and west of NYC potentially briefing going to all snow
before all precipitation tapers off.

.KEY MESSAGE 3...
Localized minor coastal flooding and localized beach erosion remain 
possible with this system given the expected magnitude of southerly 
flow and associated wave action. Astronomical tides will be rising 
early next week due to the approaching new moon. Tides are low, so 
it will take a significant surge to achieve widespread minor coastal 
flooding, which is not expected at this time as guidance has 
remained nearly steady to slightly lower over the last 24 hours. And 
surge remains at around 1/2 to 1 foot. The main concern for any 
localized minor coastal flooding continues to be with the most 
vulnerable locations of the south shore back Bays of Nassau, and 
western Great South Bay during times of high tide Monday and Monday 
night.


.KEY MESSAGE 4...
Colder airmass settles into the region with trough moving
across Tuesday before shifting farther north on Wednesday. High
pressure starts to build in Tuesday and moves directly overhead
on Wednesday. 

The forecast highs only reach near 40s and apparent temperatures
stay in the 30s for their max values. Breezy conditions Tuesday
will subside partially Wednesday.


&&

.AVIATION /07Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
High pressure over the area passes to the east on today. A strong 
frontal system will impact the area tonight through Monday night. 

Mainly VFR. MVFR develops 03-06Z Monday with a chance of rain.

Winds light northerly at the NYC metro terminals. Winds become NE 
toward the AM push, possibly becoming light and variable. At the 
outlying terminals winds remain light and variable. This  morning NE 
winds become E/SE in the afternoon with gusts up to 20 kt. There is 
a chance that gusts are more occasional before ending during the 
evening. LLWS develops toward 03Z Monday along the coast.


 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Wind direction may be more variable for the Sun AM push.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY... 

Late tonight: IFR, LIFR possible, with showers. A chance of 
thunderstorms toward daybreak. SE wind gusts near 20 kt, increasing 
to near 30 kt by daybreak Monday. Southerly LLWS at the coastal 
terminals.

Monday: IFR or lower, with rain, heavy at times in the afternoon and 
early evening. A chance of thunderstorms. Winds become southerly 
early, with gusts 30-40 kt, highest at the coast. Peak gusts up to 
45 kt possible along the coast late day into the evening. LLWS into 
the evening. Winds decrease slightly and become more westerly late 
Monday night, gusts 25-35 kt. Rain tapers off, possibly mixing with 
snow as it does so.

Tuesday: Rain/snow ends early in the morning. MVFR or lower possible 
early, improving to VFR by afternoon. WSW gusts 25 to 30 kt.

Wednesday-Thursday: VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Initially, sub-SCA on forecast waters. Then for tonight, SCA
potential rises. Gales looking more probable Monday into Monday
night. Storm force winds also possible for some time Monday
night. 

SCA conditions on most waters Tuesday and then just the ocean
through midweek.

&&
